hypotheses.rationale: orders error rate spiked to 8.11% (ALR-001) with a sharp rise in the orders/error_rate series (MET-00013, MET-01738, max 0.3924). A deployment of orders v3.6.7 'Update translations' by ben.t at 11:06:50Z (DPL-002) precedes the alert at 11:31:25Z, and orders ERROR logs (LOG-00316, LOG-01222) appear in the same window. Timing and service match strongly point to the deployment as the trigger.

A config change exists on payments (CFG-003) and orders depends on payments (DEP-004), so a payments config error could surface as orders errors. However, payments error-rate stayed low (MET-00019, MET-00042, MET-00065) and no payments ERROR logs were observed, making this unlikely.
A config change exists on auth (CFG-001) and orders depends on auth (DEP-003). But auth/error_rate stayed low (MET-00007, MET-00375, MET-00720, max 0.0036), contradicting an auth-side fault.

api-gateway had deployments (DPL-001, DPL-003) and calls orders (DEP-002), but the error signal is concentrated in orders itself, not the gateway, so a gateway deployment is unlikely to be the root cause.

recommended_remediation: Roll back orders to the previous stable release (pre-v3.6.7) to restore baseline error rate
After rollback, verify orders/error_rate (MET-00013, MET-01738) returns below the 5% threshold
Investigate the v3.6.7 'Update translations' change and re-release with a fix after regression testing
